name: Executive or regulator impersonation issuing an urgent payment order
description: A message impersonates a senior executive ('boss scam') or a regulator and instructs the recipient — typically finance staff — to make an urgent transfer, often after an account/WhatsApp takeover. The combination of a senior-identity claim, an out-of-band payment order and urgency is the signal; none of the three alone is.

source_references.document_ref: PIB PRID 2276809 — regulatory/executive impersonation for WhatsApp takeover

manual_retrieval.notes: Original automated retrieval was HTTP 403 (SRC-022 stays RETRIEVAL_FAILED). The PIB/MHA release describes regulator impersonation, urgent compliance pretexts, WhatsApp takeover and immediate transfer instructions to finance staff.

explanation.plain: Someone claiming to be your boss or a regulator is telling you to transfer money urgently. Genuine executives and regulators do not order urgent transfers through chat messages. Verify by contacting the person on a number you already trust before doing anything.
explanation.technical: Senior-identity claim (executive/regulator) + payment order + urgency/secrecy, spanning identity, payment and pressure classes. PIB/MHA documents this 'boss scam' pattern including WhatsApp takeover and immediate transfer instructions.
verification_steps: Call the executive or regulator back on a previously known official number — never the number in the message.
Confirm any transfer request through your organisation's established finance-approval channel.

provenance.notes: Sole basis SRC-022 was HTTP 403 under automated retrieval (G-03) and the rule was UNSUPPORTED at Phase 1. Manually retrieved 2026-08-15 (MR-EVID-004) and verified as exact PIB primary under DEC-006 / ADR-0015. Promoted from UNSUPPORTED to SUPPORTED (RESEARCH-004 §9).
